slides.title: Line Plots: The Classic Trend View 📉
slides.content:
# Show Change Over Time

Line plots are ideal for **time series** data: stock prices, temperatures, sales over months. You can plot multiple columns on the same axes to compare trends.

Let's work with a DataFrame of quarterly revenue.

slides.title: Multiple Lines 🎨
slides.content:
## Plot All Numeric Columns

```python
quarters.plot()
```
Each numeric column gets its own line with a distinct color. The index (dates) is used for the x‑axis.

quizData.question: If a DataFrame has 4 numeric columns, how many lines will `df.plot()` create?
quizData.explanation: Each numeric column becomes a separate line.

slides.title: Styling Lines 🖌️
slides.content:
## `style` Parameter

You can apply a style string to a column when selecting it:

```python
quarters['Revenue'].plot(style='r--')  # red dashed line
```

Common styles:
- `'b'` – blue solid
- `'g--'` – green dashed
- `'ro-'` – red circle markers with solid line
- `'k.'` – black dots

You can also pass a list of styles to a DataFrame plot: `df.plot(style=['-','--'])`

slides.title: Adding Markers 📌
slides.content:
## Emphasize Data Points

Use the `marker` parameter to add markers on each data point (e.g., `marker='o'`, `marker='s'`, `marker='^'`).

```python
df.plot(marker='o')
```

Alternatively, you can include the marker in the style string (e.g., `'o-'`).

slides.title: Area Plots 📶
slides.content:
## Fill the Area Under the Line

`kind='area'` creates a stacked area chart (by default). Useful for showing cumulative totals or proportions.

```python
quarters.plot(kind='area')
```

Use `stacked=False` for unstacked (overlapping) areas.

quizData.question: What does `stacked=False` do in an area plot?

options.text: Areas are drawn on top of each other (non‑stacked)

quizData.explanation: `stacked=False` makes the areas overlap (starting from the baseline).

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Subplots for Multiple Series

Use `subplots=True` to put each column in its own subplot: `df.plot(subplots=True, layout=(2,1), figsize=(8,6))`.
